subject: Post-demo: shortlist, fallback plan, and prompt set deliverables
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Romero <alex.romero@nimbus-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo recap: immediate asks and next steps

Hi Marissa / Karthik,

Thanks again for joining the demo with Nimbus this morning — Alex was on the call and seemed most focused on latency at 95th percentile, cost per 1M tokens, and safeguards for quality regressions when we move to quantized variants. Quick recap and asks: 

- Goal: replace existing in-house endpoint for query enrichment (expected 120 rps steady-state, spiky up to 800 rps).
- Primary constraints: 95th-pctl latency < 220ms, per-1M-token cost target <$85 (USD), privacy: no customer text stored outside VPC during Private deployment phase.
- Desired deliverables from our side: recommended shortlist of 2–3 model variants with tradeoff rationale (latency/cost/quality), a prompt set (10 canonical prompts + edge cases) for their QA, and a simple fallback policy (model downgrade + region failover).

Can you draft a one-page shortlist with the suggested model + quantization choices and a link to the benchmark CSV? I attached the raw CLI benchmark they asked for in case you want to annotate it.

Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0163

Attachments: nimbus_benchmarks_v1.csv (csv)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Romero <alex.romero@nimbus-analytics.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: shortlist + rationale (first draft)

Ben / Karthik / Alex —

Draft attached: high-level shortlist and rationale. Summary here so Alex can see the headline without opening the doc: 

Recommended shortlist (priority order):
1) rw-large-fp16 (hosted/dedicated) — highest quality baseline, 95%ile latency ~200ms on dedicated 8xA100 (no quant). Cost: estimated $120 / 1M tokens (baseline).
2) rw-medium-llm-q4_0 (dedicated with Q4 quant) — good quality preservation on enrichment tasks, 95%ile latency ~150ms, cost: ~$62 / 1M tokens. Slightly higher tokenization overhead observed on long contexts.
3) rw-medium-llm-int8-opt (dedicated/private, INT8 path) — best cost ~$48 / 1M tokens and 95%ile ~180ms, but we flagged two prompt types where hallucination risk increased (see prompt-suite annotations).

Fallback policy (proposed):
- Primary: rw-medium-llm-q4_0 in us-west region (meets latency and cost targets).
- If per-minute CPU/GPU queue > 75% or 95%ile latency spikes above 300ms for 3 consecutive minutes -> degrade to rw-medium-llm-int8-opt for throughput relief.
- If degradation leads to quality drop > 8% on the regression tests -> auto-failover to rw-large-fp16 in a neighboring region (US-EAST) and signal ops.

Notes on quality regressions: we ran the provided prompt set (attached) against the three variants and measured F1/ROUGE-like scoring for extraction tasks. INT8 variant had two failure classes: (1) numeric normalization errors in financial extractions; (2) truncated sequences for long-context prompts. Both are fixable via prompt engineering and a per-prompt post-filter (see comments in prompt_suite_v1.zip).

Next steps I propose:
- Karthik: short kernel-level notes on quantization risk and mitigation (1–2 bullets).
- Ben: share the shortlist doc and Drive link with Alex, ask for acceptance of the fallback policy or preferences on cross-region failover.
- Alex: if acceptable, I'll prepare a quick scoring matrix and a draft mutual action plan for signatures.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0202

Attachments: prompt_suite_v1.zip (contains: canonical_prompts.txt, edge_cases.csv, annotations.md)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Alex Romero <alex.romero@nimbus-analytics.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 11:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: kernel notes on quant & perf (short)

TL;DR: Q4 quant looks like the best operational sweet spot for Nimbus' workload; INT8 yields more token-level noise we saw in the tests.

More detail: 
- Q4 (rw-medium-llm-q4_0): small degradation in subjective QA (~2.5% on our extraction suite) but large gains in throughput and memory headroom. Safe to use as primary with per-prompt regression checks.
- INT8 path: inconsistent handling of 64-bit integers and long-runner history attention; this caused the numeric normalization issues Marissa flagged. We can mitigate this by (a) selective FP16 pins for the normalization layer, or (b) running a lightweight normalization post-pass in their service. Both add engineering overhead; option (a) reduces cost savings ~6–8%.
- Latency numbers: our dedicated 8xA100 numbers are congruent with Marissa's summary. Hosted runs on mixed GPUs will see 15–20% higher 95p latency; recommend Dedicated for initial rollout.

I'll add a one-paragraph snippet to the shortlist doc about the selective FP16 pin strategy and tag the benchmark rows that show the numbers.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Lead Inference Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: shortlist, fallback plan, and prompt set deliverables

Thanks team — this is super helpful. A few quick clarifications from Nimbus: 

1) The cost target of <$85 / 1M tokens is flexible if latency and quality are rock-solid. If we go with rw-medium-llm-q4_0 as primary, can you give a short run-rate estimate including reserved capacity pricing vs on-demand? (we prefer predictable monthly bills).
2) For the INT8 variant: Alex (product) asked whether the selective FP16 pin strategy would be turnkey from Redwood or if it requires engineering changes on their side.
3) Prompt set: can you isolate the 3 edge-case prompts that triggered numeric normalization issues so our QA team can run additional checks?

If you can reply with (A) a 1-paragraph cost delta (reserved vs. on-demand) and (B) a short note on who owns the FP16 pin rollout, we can move to an internal approval and schedule a short MOPs call next week.

Appreciate it — Alex
Alex Romero
Head of Product, Nimbus Analytics
alex.romero@nimbus-analytics.com
